newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria April consumer prices fall 0.7 pct m/m.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria April consumer prices fall 0.7 pct m/m.

text.p: Bulgaria's consumer prices fell 0.7 percent month on month in April after rising by 12.3 percent in March and soaring by 242.7 percent in February, National Statistics Insitute (NSI) figures showed on Saturday.
The April year on year inflation figure is expected to be released by the NSI later this month.

"Inflation slowed down below zero last month for the first time since Bulgaria launched market reforms in 1990," a NSI official told Reuters.

Prices fell mainly due to the lev's rise against the dollar on the domestic market as macroeconomic performance improved after the interim cabinet took office in mid-February and Bulgaria got pledges of $1.2 billion support from international lenders.
The lev gained from 1,588.8 per dollar on March 31 to 1,450 at end-April in the central bank fixing. It traded at 1,500 on Saturday.
"Sharp price hikes we saw in the first two months of this year due to the drastic lev fall now have begun to reverse with the strengthening of the lev," said the official.
The lev sank to all-time lows of 3,000-3,200 to the dollar in mid-February amid political uncertainty, from around 500 at the beginning of the year.

The interim cabinet recently liberalised food and fuel prices in line with recommendations made by the International Monetary Fund prior to introduction of a fixed exchange rate regime, but prices have not risen.

"The inflationary potential of the lev/dollar exchange rate has been exhausted for the time being. If the lev keeps stable we can expect stable prices in the next couple of months", the official said.
-- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188
